author: DPA
title: Hamas hands over another body to Red Cross in Gaza Strip - NewsBreak
text:
By DPA ,
2 hours ago
The Palestinian militant group Hamas has handed over another body to employees of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) in the Gaza Strip.
According to Hamas, the remains are those of a hostage kidnapped from Israel. The Red Cross employees are on their way to representatives of the Israeli military with a coffin, the military said.
The identity must then be confirmed at a forensic institute in Tel Aviv.
Israel and Hamas agreed to the exchange of bodies as part of a ceasefire agreement brokered by the United States.
According to the agreement, for each Israeli hostage whose remains are released, Israel must hand over the bodies of 15 Gaza Strip residents. The exact circumstances of the Palestinians' deaths are unknown, but it is suspected that Israel stored their bodies in a military camp.
According to the Hamas-run health authority, Israel has so far handed over 285 deceased Palestinians, of whom 84 have been identified.
On Tuesday evening, Hamas handed over the body of an Israeli soldier, who was also a German citizen, to Red Cross staff. Israel subsequently transferred 15 Palestinians' remains on Wednesday.
As part of the agreement, Hamas released all remaining living hostages on October 13 in exchange for hundreds of Palestinian prisoners.
Despite the ceasefire, violent incidents have continued in the war-torn territory.
Israel's military reported on Wednesday that it attacked two Palestinians within a military-controlled area in northern Gaza.
In both instances, the individuals approached soldiers "in a manner that posed a threat to them," the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) stated. "Following their identification, IDF troops eliminated the terrorists in order to remove the threat."
Both individuals reportedly crossed the so-called "yellow line," behind which the Israeli military has withdrawn as part of the agreed ceasefire. There were no immediate reports from Gaza regarding the incidents.
Since the ceasefire began on October 10, more than 240 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza, according to the Hamas-controlled health authority.
The claims from both sides cannot be independently verified.
